test_title: PYST 6: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Shivangi bought two varieties of pulses, costing Rs. 50 per kg and Rs. 60 per kg each, and mixed them in some ratio. Then she sold the mixture at Rs. 70 per kg. Making a profit of 20 percent. What was the ratio of the mixture?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean CP of the mixture = SP ÷ Multiplying Factor = 70 ÷ 1.2 = 175/3.

Using Alligation: (Higher CP − Mean CP) : (Mean CP − Lower CP).

Ratio = (60 − 175/3) : (175/3 − 50) = 5/3 : 25/3.

Ratio = 1 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of Variety 1 (CP₁) = ₹50/kg

Cost of Variety 2 (CP₂) = ₹60/kg

Selling Price of Mixture (SPₘᵢₓ) = ₹70/kg

Profit Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP × [100 / (100 + Profit%)]

Alligation Ratio = (CP₂ − CPₘₑₐₙ) : (CPₘₑₐₙ − CP₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/417822cefa64bf1e6eb5a58675946f807aa2bd4bb97cec037c050415dd83517e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost Price of the mixture (CPₘₑₐₙ) = 70 × (100 / 120)

⇒ CPₘₑₐₙ = 70 × (5 / 6) = 350 / 6 = ₹175/3 per kg

⇒ Applying the Rule of Alligation:

⇒ Quantity of Variety 1 / Quantity of Variety 2 = (60 − 175/3) / (175/3 − 50)

⇒ Ratio = [(180 − 175) / 3] / [(175 − 150) / 3]

⇒ Ratio = (5 / 3) / (25 / 3)

⇒ Ratio = 5 / 25 = 1 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is 1:5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at the given price must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price.

Cost Price Calculation

While applying alligation, always ensure all values are in the same unit (all CP or all SP). CP = SP ÷ (1 + Profit%).

Mean Value

The mean value of a mixture always lies between the values of the cheaper and the dearer ingredients (CP₁ < CPₘₑₐₙ < CP₂).
